doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Leaving Coltrane: Blakey, Ellington and big bands
title: The 'starvation band' and thoughts of driving a cab
summary: Woody Shaw's remark about hard times is discussed; Aisha confirms lean years and Tyner says cab driving was only a thought.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: OK, well I’m glad we cleared that up, but I do have a quote from Woody Shaw saying that there was a lack of work at this time because he was working in your group and I guess he said jokingly that they called your band the “starvation band.” I guess times were pretty hard at that point?
Well I would say this is around late 60’s early 70’s before you got with Milestone, because Milestone, that launches a whole other epoch in your career.
Yeah, Orrin [Keepnews] was a good guy.
So we’ll talk about that, but was that accurate? It was a rough time.
And one other quote said that he was entertaining the idea of driving a cab. I know Sunny Murray went back to Philadelphia and drove a cab too so I thought, well maybe this-
And you can call your own hours.
Exactly (laughs) No, I actually didn’t get that involved with the cab driving, it was a thought.
Yeah, it was just a thought.
You know that’s a part of life.
